notes: Both address di-nucleosome binding hypothesis (C114-C116). LLM considers it a reasonable structural inference requiring validation, while peer reviewers explicitly reject it as 'highly speculative' due to histone tail flexibility, requesting removal from discussion.

Both agree AEBP2's allosteric role (C7) and stabilization mechanism are interpretive rather than definitively demonstrated. LLM notes it requires functional validation; peer reviewers call these inferences 'speculative given the resolution.'

Both agree regulatory mechanisms (C104-C108, C111, C113) are reasonable inferences but remain speculative. LLM notes they require functional validation; peer reviewers state 'inferences about biochemical function are speculative given the resolution.'

Partial overlap on histone-tail binding regions (C8, C9, C70, C75, C102, C103). LLM supports localization claims as well-supported by structural data. Peer review groups these with broader mechanistic claims (C96-C113) and considers all speculative, creating disagreement on the subset.

Both support cross-linking/MS interaction mapping (C42-C59 overlap). LLM validates methodology and consistency with crystal structures; peer reviewers affirm 'cross-linking experiments confirm the structural conclusions.'

Both support the 3D EM structure determination (C5, C36-C39, C121-C126 overlap). LLM validates methodology and structural homogeneity; peer reviewers affirm 'conclusions about shape and location are sound and convincing' and 'work is of very high quality.'

Both address sample heterogeneity and particle selection (C23-C25, C31). LLM supports the stabilization approach as validated by improved class averages. Peer reviewers express concern about heterogeneous populations and request clarification on particle rejection criteria.

Both support reconstitution strategy and complex quality (C22, C28-C30, C32-C35). LLM validates biochemical homogeneity and cross-linking approach; peer reviewers affirm overall work quality and structural conclusions.

Both support EED WD40 localization to Lobe A (C40, C60-C61, C65-C66, C68-C69). LLM validates internal tagging method and consistency with crystal structure; peer reviewers affirm 'location of different subunits' conclusions are 'sound and convincing.'

Both support AEBP2 chain path determination (C82-C86). LLM validates multiple tags and cross-linking data; peer reviewers affirm cross-linking confirms structural conclusions and subunit organization.
Both support Ezh2 domain localization (C76-C79). LLM validates internal GFP tagging and cross-linking consistency; peer reviewers affirm cross-linking confirms structural conclusions.

Both address RCT methodology (C124). LLM supports the approach as appropriate for structure determination. Peer reviewers question why only 20 classes were used, noting this 'would lead to rather poor resolution' and request justification.

Both address Suz12 chain path (C80-C81). LLM considers it speculative with limited tagging data, noting 'most likely' indicates uncertainty. Peer reviewers support overall subunit organization conclusions as 'sound and convincing.'

Both support stoichiometry determination (C87-C88). LLM validates single copy observation across tagging experiments; peer reviewers affirm 'location of different subunits and relative orientation' conclusions.
Both support RbAp48 WD40 localization to Lobe D (C73-C74). LLM validates indirect tagging and crystal structure docking; peer reviewers affirm subunit location conclusions are 'sound and convincing.'

Both support comprehensive architectural model (C6, C89). LLM validates convergent evidence from multiple techniques; peer reviewers affirm 'conclusions supported by redundant and accurate information' and work is 'very significant advance.'

Both support background context and utility claims (C90, C118-C120 in LLM; C1-C4, C10-C21, C26-C27, C62, C67, C91-C93, C110 in peer). These contextual claims about PRC2 importance and prior knowledge are accepted by both.
